source_refs.note: Exercise 4.3, Question 6: book page 77 (PDF 82); answer key PDF 303

blocks.prompt: 6 (i) Solve the following system of homogeneous linear equations by using Gaussian elimination method: \(x + 4x - 2z = 0\), \(2x + y + 5z = 0\), \(5x + 2y + 8z = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
The first equation is printed with a misprint (\(4x\) for \(4y\)); we solve \(x + 4y - 2z = 0\).
A homogeneous system: all constants are 0.
We must decide whether only \((0, 0, 0)\) works or infinitely many solutions exist, and find them.
Plan: echelon form, count the rank, compare with 3, back substitute.
steps:
Given (with the misprint corrected, see the Book correction below): \(x + 4y - 2z = 0\), \(2x + y + 5z = 0\), \(5x + 2y + 8z = 0\)
To find: all solutions by Gaussian elimination.
Method: Reduce the augmented matrix to echelon form. A homogeneous system always has the trivial solution \((0, 0, 0)\). If rank of \(A\) = 3 (number of variables) that is the only solution; if rank \(< 3\) there are infinitely many (non-trivial) solutions.

Augmented matrix
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 8 & 0\end{array}\right]\]
Why: The last column is all zeros because every equation equals 0.

Put the row with leading 1 second
By \(R_2 \leftrightarrow R_3\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -7 & 9 & 0\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Now row 2 has a ready leading 1.

Leading 1 in row 3
By \(\frac{1}{2}R_3 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0\), \(0\), \(1\) | \(0\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]\]
Why: Dividing by 2. Echelon form: three non-zero rows.

Rank and solution
Rank of \(A\) = 3 = number of variables. The echelon form stands for
\[x + 4y - 2z = 0\]
\[y - z = 0\]
\[z = 0\]
Back substitution: \(z = 0\), then \(y = z = 0\), then \(x = -4y + 2z = 0\).
Why: Rule I: when the rank equals the number of variables, a homogeneous system has only the trivial solution.

Check with the determinant
\[|A| = 1(8 - 10) - 4(16 - 25) - 2(4 - 5)\]
\[= -2 + 36 + 2 = 36\]
Why: \(|A| \neq 0\) is the same as rank 3, so only \((0, 0, 0)\) works.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the first equation of 6(i) as \(x + 4x - 2z = 0\). It should read \(x + 4y - 2z = 0\): each equation of the system has \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\), and the answer key's \(\{(0, 0, 0)\}\) fits this equation (\(|A| = 36 \neq 0\)). Even taken literally (\(5x - 2z = 0\)) the determinant is \(-8 \neq 0\), so the answer, only the trivial solution, is the same.

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) Solve the following system of homogeneous linear equations by using Gaussian elimination method: \(x_1 + 4x_2 + 2x_3 = 0\), \(2x_1 + x_2 - 3x_3 = 0\), \(3x_1 + 2x_2 - 4x_3 = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
A homogeneous system: all constants are 0.
We must decide whether only \((0, 0, 0)\) works or infinitely many solutions exist, and find them.
Plan: echelon form, count the rank, compare with 3, back substitute.
steps:
Given: \(x_1 + 4x_2 + 2x_3 = 0\), \(2x_1 + x_2 - 3x_3 = 0\), \(3x_1 + 2x_2 - 4x_3 = 0\)
To find: all solutions by Gaussian elimination.
Method: Reduce the augmented matrix to echelon form. A homogeneous system always has the trivial solution \((0, 0, 0)\). If rank of \(A\) = 3 (number of variables) that is the only solution; if rank \(< 3\) there are infinitely many (non-trivial) solutions.

Augmented matrix
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & -4 & 0\end{array}\right]\]
Why: The last column is all zeros because every equation equals 0.

Rank and the reduced system
Rank of \(A\) = 2 < 3 = number of variables. The echelon form stands for
\[x_1 + 4x_2 + 2x_3 = 0\]
\[x_2 + x_3 = 0\]
\[0x_3 = 0\]
Why: Rule II: rank less than the number of variables means infinitely many (non-trivial) solutions; one variable is free.

Let \(x_3 = t\) and back substitute
\[x_2 = -t\]
\[x_1 = -4(-t) - 2t\]
\[x_1 = 2t\]
Why: From the second equation \(x_2 = -t\); put it in the first equation and solve for \(x_1\).

Check in the original equations
\[(2t) + 4(-t) + 2(t) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[2(2t) + (-t) - 3(t) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[3(2t) + 2(-t) - 4(t) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The general solution satisfies every equation for any \(t\). For example \(t = 1\) gives \((2, -1, 1)\).
blocks.final_answer: \(x_1 = 2t,\ x_2 = -t,\ x_3 = t\) for any value of \(t\)

blocks.prompt: 6 (iii) Solve the following system of homogeneous linear equations by using Gaussian elimination method: \(x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 = 0\), \(x_1 - x_2 + 5x_3 = 0\), \(2x_1 + x_2 + 4x_3 = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
A homogeneous system: all constants are 0.
We must decide whether only \((0, 0, 0)\) works or infinitely many solutions exist, and find them.
Plan: echelon form, count the rank, compare with 3, back substitute.
steps:
Given: \(x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 = 0\), \(x_1 - x_2 + 5x_3 = 0\), \(2x_1 + x_2 + 4x_3 = 0\)
To find: all solutions by Gaussian elimination.
Method: Reduce the augmented matrix to echelon form. A homogeneous system always has the trivial solution \((0, 0, 0)\). If rank of \(A\) = 3 (number of variables) that is the only solution; if rank \(< 3\) there are infinitely many (non-trivial) solutions.

Augmented matrix
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 0\end{array}\right]\]
Why: The last column is all zeros because every equation equals 0.

Rank and the reduced system
Rank of \(A\) = 2 < 3 = number of variables. The echelon form stands for
\[x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 = 0\]
\[x_2 - 2x_3 = 0\]
\[0x_3 = 0\]
Why: Rule II: rank less than the number of variables means infinitely many (non-trivial) solutions; one variable is free.

Let \(x_3 = t\) and back substitute
\[x_2 = 2t\]
\[x_1 = -2(2t) + 1t\]
\[x_1 = -3t\]
Why: From the second equation \(x_2 = 2t\); put it in the first equation and solve for \(x_1\).

Check in the original equations
\[(-3t) + 2(2t) - (t) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[(-3t) - (2t) + 5(t) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[2(-3t) + (2t) + 4(t) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The general solution satisfies every equation for any \(t\). For example \(t = 1\) gives \((-3, 2, 1)\).
blocks.final_answer: \(x_1 = -3t,\ x_2 = 2t,\ x_3 = t\) for any value of \(t\)
